requirements.summary: Create and publish the infrastructure in the named GitHub repository.
Use DeepSeek Harness as effectively as practical.
Build the development infrastructure now, not the catalog application.
Enable an agent to ingest evidence, implement from specifications, verify, and deliver software.
Divide the future catalog work into multiple specifications.
Use the supplied ProductEntry JSON and catalog SQLite URLs as future system inputs.
Track and map cost to every repository change.
Run OpenAI models through DeepSeek Harness and price OpenAI usage.
Receive a file containing products supplied by multiple sellers.
Persist consolidated results into the supplied SQLite catalog.
Do not insert a duplicate product; link the existing product to the seller.
Database changes are allowed when justified.
Intentional ambiguities and defensible reasoning matter more than production scale.
The candidate delivery is time-bounded and hosted in a public repository.
The candidate must validate AI output and explain decisions, limitations, and trade-offs.
The JSON snapshot has 269 rows, five stable fields, nullable brands, and seller-scoped identity concerns.
The SQLite snapshot has 975 Product rows, zero SellerProduct rows, and two application tables.
Incoming IDs are opaque strings while SellerProductId is declared INTEGER.
The fixtures contain duplicate IDs, formatting and language variations, and injection-shaped text.
